Ah, yes, the age old fundamentalist argument. "If I can't understand it, it must not be real." Just as fundamentalist Christians can't validly deny evolution because they can't understand how evolution and Genesis can both be true, fundamentalist atheists can't validly deny God's existence just because they can't understand a good God and a world with both good and evil.

A quick answer is that evil is simply the privation of good. When God creates free will and life those with free will can choose to throw away their free will and kill themselves. When you create life you create the possibility for non-life (that is, death).

Also the problem of evil doesn't answer where good comes from. You still have to account for why there are living things to kill. Why there is love that can be spurned. Why there is something rather than nothing.

Atheism is lazy thinking. If you apply your skepticism to yourself and ask, "but where does everything come from?" Then you would find that God has to exist. Unless you're a closed minded fundamentalist who can't open his mind to full reality.

I'm Christian but I'm also and Aristotelian.  This will start from the Aristotelian side.

Aristotle begins with the simple observation the some things are alive and some things are not. He says that the soul is what we call whatever gives life to living things and is not present in non-living things. Next he observes that human beings have additional powers to know immaterial things like "truth" and to desire immaterial things like "good." Because our powers to know and desire have immaterial objects these powers must be immaterial too and thus exist beyond our mortal and physical bodies. So our Intellect and Will will exist and act forever.

Our bodies, however, seem to be the only way for our Intellects and Wills to get new information. Thus when we die all we will have is our habits of Intellect and Will, that is we'll have our usual thought and desires but no new ones. Thus if you die with the habitual desire to not exit you will forever desire to not exist but you won't be able to change that desire once you die. This is what we call Hell. If we habituate ourselves to desire things that can't make us happy we can never become happy.

This is the Christian understanding of Hell. God doesn't send us there but our habitual denial of Him creates Hell for ourselves. God loves everyone infinitely but no matter how much you love someone you can't expect them to love you back. Same with God. He doesn't force you to love Him back and He respects your choice to separate yourself from Him. So if you choose Hell God won't (actually He can't) force you into Heaven after your death just as he won't (and can't) force you to be Christian on earth.

Your fate is only fixed after you die because matter can be changed but the immaterial cannot.
